thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SRE on-call (sachi) — alert: sudden 5xx spike on /v1/generate for models using prefix cache. Sev=2. 1770123456

sachi: saw it. getting logs now. can someone drop tracing link?

mike: paging in channel. link: https://internal.trace/redwood/trace/0xabc123 (full traces show KV cache writes exploding)

rachel: symptoms: request latency jumps from 80ms to 900ms, error rate 12% -> 503s. Most traces show repeated KV writes for the same prompt prefix.

sachi: looks like prefix hashing changed after last prompt-template deploy. tokenizer mapping drift + new batching config = runaway cache keys.

jin: confirmation: continuous-batching enabled in dedicated pools 10m ago (autobatch window=50ms). With the new hash seed the same prefix gets slightly different tokenization, creating near-unique cache keys each request -> massive cache cardinality.

mike: impact: 3 enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, FinlyPay, NudgeAI) hit elevated tail latencies and rate-limited errors. Cust-ops notified.

cust-ops: we've opened support tickets and told customers we're investigating; giving ETA ~30m.

sachi: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching on affected pools 2) increase prefix-cache TTL from 24h -> 5m (reduce build-up) 3) run targeted cache prune for pathological prefixes 4) rollback tokenization seed change if needed.

rachel: I can flip batching off on dedicated-prod-pool-3 now. doing it.

(small bot): deploy-bot: disable-autobatch on dedicated-prod-pool-3 accepted by infra; roll started.

sachi: after disabling, I'm seeing KV write rate drop 10x. latency improving but still noisy.

mike: preparing PR for hotfix: revert tokenizer-seed change (commit 4f3a2e7). Holding for canary verification.

jin: we should avoid full global cache flush — that would hurt warmed prefixes. I'll run a targeted prune for keys matching prefix-hash pattern for the new seed.

sachi: commands to run (I'll execute with ops perms):

```
# list top keys by write rate
redis-cli -h redis-prod --eval scripts/top_prefix_writes.lua
# delete new-seed keys (prefix newseed_*)
redis-cli -h redis-prod KEYS "newseed_*" | xargs -r redis-cli -h redis-prod DEL
# temporarily lower TTL
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/cache/ttl -d '{"scope":"prefix_cache","ttl_secs":300}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

mike: running the KEYS+DEL now on shard-2. progress: 40% (taking care to iterate, not blocking).

rachel: can we also add a fallback: on cache miss if count(prefix_variants) > 20 then skip caching for that prefix to avoid re-entrance?

jin: yes, will patch runtime to short-circuit caching for high-cardinality prefixes; quick change in 5m.

sachi: rolling rollback PR to canary (revert 4f3a2e7). canary target is 5% traffic for 10 minutes.

deploy-bot: canary deploy initiated by mike -> canary-1 (5%).

(10m pass)

sachi: canary looks good, error rate back to baseline on canary traces. proceeding to full rollback in stages.

mike: full rollback completed. continuous batching remains disabled until we validate changes. KV write rate back to normal.

cust-ops: update: customers notified of rollback and mitigation; monitoring pinged them. AcmeCorp confirms degraded behavior cleared.

oncall-rotation: handoff note for next on-call (jin): monitor prefix cache cardinality metrics, tokenization mismatch alerts, and batching.autowindow changes.

jin: on it. next steps (post-incident):
- add a safety gate: reject tokenizer-seed changes without a compatibility test that ensures stable prefix hashes for a sample of prompts
- add metric: prefix_cache_unique_keys_per_min per model & per template
- implement high-cardinality short-circuit in runtime
- add a playbook entry for "prefix-hash drift"

mike: also add automated canary job: when template or tokenizer changes are merged, run a quick job to detect >5% changed prefix hashes across a corpus.

sachi: severity downgrade to P2. writing postmortem. immediate RCA: tokenizer seed update + more aggressive batching together created >1M near-unique cache keys in hours, causing Redis eviction pressure and request slowdowns.

rachel: tagging infra and eng-runtime for follow-up. I'll create tasks in our incident tracker with owners.

cust-ops: customers want a short write-up for the incident and what prevented recurrence. I'll draft and share.

sachi: thanks everyone. handoff complete to jin for next 8h watch. please add any missing notes to the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
